plasma_membrane.name: Plasma Membrane (Cell Membrane)
plasma_membrane.description: Flexible outer phospholipid bilayer with embedded receptor proteins controlling nutrient entry and waste elimination without a rigid cell wall.

golgi_apparatus.name: Golgi Apparatus (Packaging Cisternae)
golgi_apparatus.description: Stacks of flattened saccules and budding transport vesicles that chemically modify, glycosylate, and package secretory proteins.

endoplasmic_reticulum.name: Endoplasmic Reticulum (Rough & Smooth)
endoplasmic_reticulum.description: Continuous network of folded cisternae; Rough ER is coated with ribosomes for export protein synthesis, while Smooth ER synthesizes steroids and lipids.

cytoplasm.name: Cytoplasm (Cytosol)
cytoplasm.description: Gel-like cytoplasmic matrix containing metabolic enzymes, soluble proteins, and cytoskeletal filaments maintaining cellular shape.

centrosome_centrioles.name: Centrosome with Centrioles
centrosome_centrioles.description: Pair of perpendicular microtubule barrels that organize the mitotic spindle apparatus during animal cell division.

nucleus.name: Nucleus (Chromatin & Double Envelope)
nucleus.description: Double-membraned organelle perforated with nuclear pores containing chromosomal DNA and controlling cellular gene transcription.

nucleolus.name: Nucleolus
nucleolus.description: Dense non-membrane enclosed region within the nucleoplasm responsible for transcribing ribosomal RNA and assembling ribosomal subunits.

lysosome.name: Lysosome (Digestive Hydrolases)
lysosome.description: Membrane-bound spherical vesicle filled with hydrolytic digestive enzymes that break down worn-out organelles, debris, and foreign particles.

mitochondrion.name: Mitochondrion (ATP Powerhouse)
mitochondrion.description: Rod-shaped double-membrane organelle that carries out the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation to produce cellular ATP.

small_vacuoles.name: Small Temporary Vacuoles / Vesicles
small_vacuoles.description: Small, transient fluid vesicles used for storage, endocytosis, and exocytosis, contrasting with the huge permanent vacuole of plant cells.
